daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Former President Jokowi confirmed his PSI membership dates back to October 2025 and is set to become chairman of the party's advisory board in November, as he claimed political opponents are beginning to fear PSI. This development marks a significant shift in Indonesia's political landscape as the former head of state formally aligns with a parliamentary party that has been positioning itself as a reformist force.

  • Non-parliamentary parties presented divergent positions on parliamentary thresholds, with a coalition proposing a 1 percent threshold while Partai Ummat advocated for 0 percent in the election law revision, and the parties plan to meet DPR deputy speaker Dasco to discuss the matter.
  • The Ministry of Immigration and Corrections deactivated the Cibinong prison warden and four subordinates following revelations of a luxury cluster for inmates, with the ministry launching an internal investigation after alcohol and a golf simulator disappeared from the facility.
  • Ansufri Idrus Sambo was inaugurated as chairman of Partai Ummat.
  • National Police promoted 50 high-ranking officers and four civil servants, with Roycke Harry Langie elevated to commissioner general.
  • The Home Affairs Ministry urged local governments to accelerate regional regulations protecting vulnerable workers.
  • Budayawan and Marhaenis figure Guruh Soekarnoputra passed away and was buried near his mother Fatmawati, with Megawati and Pramono Anung attending the funeral at Karet Bivak.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Foreign Minister Sugiono told the UN General Assembly that Palestine is a test of the world's conscience and Indonesia will always support the Palestinian cause, while also backing a boycott of imports from illegal Israeli settlements and calling for protection of Jerusalem from Zionism. Indonesia separately called for concrete action to protect Jerusalem's status quo.

  • At the UN, Indonesia emphasized the urgency of UN reform in the 21st century, stressed national resilience, and highlighted ASEAN's success story in strengthening Southeast Asian partnerships.
  • Foreign Minister Sugiono expressed appreciation for UN Secretary-General Guterres as his term nears its end.
  • Indonesia and Burkina Faso signed a framework agreement for cooperation.
  • Indonesian Law Minister Yusril said Indonesia respects the Philippines' decision to grant a full pardon to Mary Jane Veloso, echoed by a separate ministry statement.
  • Indonesia urged concrete action to address threats from rising sea levels at the UN.

Other

Labor unions and employers identified layoffs reaching 53,000 workers with differing views on the root causes of this major employment contraction. This represents a significant challenge to Indonesia's labor market amid broader economic adjustments.

  • Bank Indonesia moved to strengthen the halal value chain for global markets, called for sharia finance reform as global competition intensifies, and urged small businesses to improve governance to access loans, while Indonesia seeks a bigger share of the US$2.6 billion global halal market.
  • Bank Indonesia expanded cross-border QRIS to boost foreign tourist spending, with inbound digital payments surging to $345 million via cross-border QR.
  • Search and rescue teams recovered 11 more bodies after a ship sank in the Java Sea.
  • A list of banks that closed in the nine months through September 25 was released.
  • The operations of a school in Rembang were temporarily halted and its head was dismissed after 105 students and 8 teachers suffered suspected food poisoning.
